podcast.title: New Wave Powerpop
podcast.body: The Vapors are mentioned as a band contributing to the new wave iteration of Powerpop. Their sound, like other contemporaries, demonstrated how Powerpop's core elements were adopted and adapted within the burgeoning alternative rock scene. "We can probably include the jam, the smiths, XTC, squeeze, and the vapors."

podcast.title: Post-Breakup Reformation
podcast.body: The Vapors broke up in 1982 but reformed in 2016 and were still playing gigs as of the transcript's date, without achieving any further significant hits. "Well they broke up in 1982, but reformed in 2016 and are still playing gigs."

xref.title: Illustrator of Album Artwork
xref.body: Martin Hanford, known as the creator of the *Where's Waldo* books, began his career as an illustrator for album artwork. An example of his earlier work can be found on the front cover of The Vapors' album, *Magnets*, where a hidden assassin is said to be present. "began his professional life as an illustrator of album artwork."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Managerial Connection
xref.body: John Weller, father of Paul Weller and manager of The Jam, played a role in pushing for The Vapors to record their hit song "Turning Japanese." "John Weller, the father of the jam's Paul Weller and manager of that band, pushed to have the Vapers recorded."

xref.title: New Wave Powerpop
xref.body: The Jam are listed as one of the bands whose music, along with other acts like The Smiths and XTC, could be included in the new wave spectrum of Powerpop. Their sound contributed to the integration of Powerpop into alternative rock, demonstrating the influence of punk. "We can probably include the jam, the smiths, XTC, squeeze, and the vapors."

xref.title: New Wave Powerpop
xref.body: The Smiths are mentioned as a band whose work aligns with the new wave interpretation of Powerpop. Their inclusion signifies the genre's broadening appeal and integration into alternative rock, showcasing diverse expressions of the hooky, melodic, and energetic sound. "We can probably include the jam, the smiths, XTC, squeeze, and the vapors."

xref.title: New Wave Powerpop
xref.body: Squeeze is included in the list of bands associated with the new wave form of Powerpop. Their work exemplifies the genre's ability to evolve and integrate into the broader alternative rock landscape of the late 1970s and early 1980s. "We can probably include the jam, the smiths, XTC, squeeze, and the vapors."
